Prime Minister Anthony Albanese will seek to reset Australia's world standing at the Commonwealth heads of government meeting in Antigua and Barbuda. Domestic pressures and a likely interest rate hike loom.
A dolphin that washed ashore on South Australia's Fleurieu Peninsula has tested positive for H5 bird flu.
A new study estimates smoke from months of Indonesian wildfires caused 3,560 deaths in September. The figure comes from the study's pollution-linked estimate.
Former president Joseph Kabila has launched a new rebel movement. The move raises questions about what it means for the Democratic Republic of Congo.
Staff at the Korowai Manaaki youth justice facility in Manurewa alerted emergency services after a small fire was detected. A young person could face charges.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney expects to conclude negotiations by June on an unprecedented deal making Canada an EU associate member. The deal is not yet concluded.
The Kangaroos beat Cook Islands 66-6 to go undefeated through the Rugby League World Cup group stage. New Zealand also beat Fiji, and the Kiwi Ferns beat Papua New Guinea.
Egypt's foreign minister says Cairo fears that escalation in the Iran war would be more destructive.
BBC Verify visits a US election centre to show how mail-in ballots for the midterm elections are secured, processed and counted.
UK Prime Minister Burnham says he is open to a formal apology for slavery but rules out financial reparations, despite long-standing Caribbean demands.
Analysis of ten key US Senate midterm races, from Texas to Maine, as rising prices and the Iran war put seats in play for Democrats.
France prepares for a third weekend of protests with about 70,000 security personnel deployed, after violence on October 17; shops have boarded up and authorities warn of clashes.
Police detained three protesters during an overnight rally as the Polish president backed a suspended judge.
Malaysia is rethinking the death penalty for drug offences, while Singapore insists its tough laws deter substance abuse.
The UN has closed its Somalia mission, ending three decades of political engagement; Somalia calls the closure a milestone amid political tensions and cuts to support.
Iran's supreme leader warns that Tehran's potential response to an attack will not be restricted by geography, as mediators try for peace.
Iranian lawmakers call for withdrawal from the NPT; observers say withdrawal would not by itself mean Iran builds a nuclear weapon.
events.disputed: Observers' view that withdrawal does not mean a weapon is an opinion, not established fact.

events.summary: Former Muslim rebel leader Abdulraof Macacua has been elected chief minister of the Philippines' Bangsamoro region.
Four oil tankers, including a supertanker carrying over two million barrels of oil, reportedly hit mines and caught fire while transiting the Strait of Hormuz.
Poland's president has accused Prime Minister Tusk of a forced takeover of the country's top court.
A new outbreak of fighting in Yemen has displaced 290,000 people, according to the UN, with pregnant women among those at risk.
Donald Trump promised to cut gasoline prices below $2 a gallon in his first year, but gasoline, diesel and jet fuel prices have instead risen.
Thai Red Cross workers dressed in Halloween costumes for a blood drive in Bangkok.
West Indies beat Bangladesh by eight wickets in the first Test in Mirpur, extending their red-ball cricket run.
Sámi communities on the Norway-Russia border face a growing divide as Russia's war in Ukraine reshapes the Arctic frontier and strains cross-border traditions.
Cryptocurrency-linked interest groups are spending over $200 million on the 2026 US midterm elections to pressure Congress for favorable rules.
Set Active founder Lindsey Carter shares how she started her athleisure company with $20K in debt from her dining room, now earning eight figures a year.
CNBC reports legal recruiter Danielle Thompson's advice for employees facing the wind-down of Weil, Gotshal & Manges and other firms undergoing dissolution.
A shooting at a Spirit Halloween store in California left 1 person dead and 6 wounded, according to police.
Al Jazeera analysis says Israel's election showed little appetite for political alternatives, with Gaza absent from the ballot despite the war and regional isolation.
events.disputed: Analysis piece; the characterization of the election and the term genocide are presented as the outlet's framing.

events.summary: Qatari mediators held more than 12 hours of talks in Tehran, per an Axios report, aiming to restart direct U.S.-Iran negotiations and avoid resumed American-led attacks on Iran.
events.disputed: Based on a single source and an Axios report; not independently confirmed in the snippet.

events.summary: South Africa's cricket team is weighing fitness news ahead of the first test against Australia. Nortje is eyeing a return after a lengthy absence, Green is ruled out, and Rabada is in contention.
events.story: south africa cricket test australia squad

events.summary: Brazil's presidential election is headed to a runoff between Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro after the first-round vote. Lula was ahead in polls before the vote, and both candidates wrapped up their campaigns.
events.story: brazil presidential election runoff lula bolsonaro

events.summary: The South African rand has moved in a narrow range, pressured at times by a stronger dollar and a local fuel price hike, and steady after weak manufacturing data. Middle East conflict and US inflation are also weighing on sentiment.
US Treasury Secretary Bessent is reported to be skipping the IMF-World Bank meetings in Bangkok, according to an exclusive Reuters report. Rain is forecast for Bangkok ahead of the meetings.
events.story: bessent skips imf world bank bangkok

events.summary: Tropical Storm Simon formed in the Pacific off Mexico's southwestern coast and strengthened into a hurricane. It threatens Mexico's tourist region.
Kenya's central bank held its key rate and said inflation is within target despite a recent rise.
Federal Reserve minutes indicate another interest rate hike is likely later this year to combat persistent inflation.
Trump said the US will not resume military strikes on Iran or attack Iran before the November 3 midterm elections.
events.story: trump no iran strikes before midterms

events.summary: Brazil's Flavio Bolsonaro vowed to keep pension increases above the inflation rate.
Houthi strikes on Riyadh airport killed three Saudis as the war escalates.
A Houthi strike on a Saudi airport reportedly killed 12 people, described as the worst attack on the kingdom in a decade. A new attack on the airport a day later reportedly killed one more person.
India's inflation rose to 5.54% in September, strengthening the case for further interest rate hikes.
Japan's wholesale inflation remains elevated, keeping alive the view that the Bank of Japan may raise rates.
Flavio Bolsonaro slightly leads Lula in a Quaest poll ahead of the Brazil runoff, though another poll shows his lead narrowing. Corruption is a top voter concern.
events.disputed: Snippets report differing poll results on who leads, so the standing is contested.

events.summary: US inflation heated up in September, and a Fed rate hike this month is back on the table, though a hike call is seen as tight.
French glassmaker Duralex has been pulled back from the brink for the fifth time in 25 years by an entrepreneur promising an environmentally conscious new chapter.
Nigeria's inflation rate eased slightly but remains a worry for many citizens.
The South African rand held steady or gained slightly as traders awaited the budget speech and inflation data.
A gold mine collapse in southwest Colombia killed at least 14 people and injured 7, according to reports. Early reports had given lower death tolls.
events.disputed: Reported death toll rose from at least 6 to 14 across snippets.

events.summary: Nigeria reported its first Ebola case as the outbreak reached West Africa, and Africa CDC called an Ebola crisis summit.
A Houthi attack on a Yemen training camp has killed 73 people, according to the reported death toll rising.
New Zealand's third-quarter inflation slowed to 3.7%, but expectations remain for an interest rate hike next week.
events.story: new zealand inflation slows rate hike

events.summary: Reuters stock price pages for several companies with 'Asia' in their names were listed, including Overseas Chinese Town, Restaurant Brands Asia, Phoenix Asia Holdings and Great Wall Pan Asia Holdings. The snippets contain no news content.
Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers in the West Bank, and Israel threatened a new offensive there.
events.story: west bank gunmen kill israeli soldiers

events.summary: Typhoon Champi swept past Taiwan, leaving one person dead and about 500 injured.
An earthquake of magnitude 6.16 struck the Vanuatu islands, according to GFZ.
Lula won Brazil's election and vowed to govern for all. Bolsonaro contests the loss and Trump called the election 'rigged' without citing evidence.
events.disputed: Trump's claim that the Brazil election was 'rigged' is made without citing evidence; Bolsonaro contests the loss while Bolsonaro's party recognizes Lula's win.

events.summary: South Africa won the third cricket test against Australia to claim the series 2-1, with Harmer shining in the win.
Flavio Bolsonaro said Brazil federal police asked for his passports and he missed a deadline to turn them in. Trump said he approves of him coming to the US.
events.disputed: Flavio Bolsonaro's account of the police request and deadline is reported by Reuters without independent confirmation in the snippets.

events.summary: Global leaders congratulated Lula on his reelection as Brazil's president, according to AP and Reuters.
Jordan carried out a deadly strike in Syria in retaliation for a church attack. Syrian health officials said the strike on a village killed five people, including women and children.
Brazil's Flavio Bolsonaro left Brazil for the US after his election defeat, according to a source and media reports. The State Department said he and his family will get US visas.
events.disputed: Reported via unnamed source and media reports.

events.summary: Trump said he will visit a tanker in Texas carrying the first oil from a Venezuela deal. Reuters reports the reality of the touted record deal is now setting in.
events.disputed: Reuters headline suggests the deal's touted record may not match reality.

events.summary: Trump said US voter fraud is rampant, while BBC Verify examines his claims as evidence suggests such fraud is extremely rare. He casts doubt on the security of the midterm elections.
events.disputed: Trump's claims of rampant voter fraud are contested by evidence suggesting it is extremely rare.

events.summary: Zambia's president appointed a new mines minister in cabinet changes following the election.

The Reserve Bank of Australia has primed markets for an interest rate rise, with a forecast that unemployment might have to move higher. Commentary says the RBA cares more about inflation than full employment.
Ethiopia says it received Russian Su-35 jets, with S-400 air defence systems to follow. The acquisition comes amid ongoing fighting in northern Tigray.
At least 68 people died in Spain's second major train crash this year. A Spanish minister refused to resign over the crash on his watch.
Thailand's defending champion Fifa Laopakdee and New Zealand's Zack Swanwick contended for the lead at the Asia-Pacific Amateur golf event in windy conditions in New Zealand.
The death toll from the Spanish train crash rose to 69 as the search for victims continued.
Israel's election has reached a deadlock with over 90% of votes counted, with analysts seeing new elections as the most likely outcome.
Uganda says 27 citizens were killed or are presumed dead after fighting for Russia in Ukraine.
EU chief Ursula von der Leyen continues to call Canada an 'associate member' of the bloc at a Montreal summit, despite opposition from some members including Germany.
events.disputed: Opposition from some EU members, including Germany, to the 'associate member' term.

events.summary: The US Federal Reserve held interest rates steady while the economy grew, a decision that affects mortgages and car loans.
Sir Patrick Stewart, English actor known for Star Trek and X-Men and for Shakespearean stage work, has died at age 86.
ECB President Christine Lagarde will step down several months early to have more freedom to engage on matters beyond monetary policy, fueling speculation about her future plans.
The US has proposed Venezuela elections for 2027, according to opposition leader Machado, who called for elections after returning from nearly a year in exile.
events.disputed: Machado's account of the US proposal and transition is presented as her statement; not independently confirmed in snippets.

events.summary: Dockworkers at more than 100 ports worldwide struck against arms shipments and war deaths.
Solomon Islands Prime Minister Wale asked the public for prayers as he recovers in Australia after being referred there for further treatment.
The Democratic Party faces an identity crisis over what it stands for and who should represent it, regardless of the midterm election result.
An ASEAN envoy met a Myanmar minister to discuss the civil war and access for aid. The outlet reported the meeting as a discussion of both issues.
events.story: asean envoy myanmar civil war talks

events.summary: France's economy unexpectedly shrank in the third quarter while inflation rose more than expected. The finance minister warned of a wall, as pressure grows ahead of further nationwide protests.

Crypto exchange Binance said about $6.3bn in digital assets was affected by a hack, thought to be the biggest crypto hack on record. Binance says it covers 90% of losses, and the FBI says North Korea was responsible.
events.disputed: Attribution to North Korea is described as suspected by analytics firms; the headline calls the hack suspected to be the largest.

events.summary: Azerbaijan's president skipped a summit hosted by Turkey. The absence has led to talk of a rift with ally Ankara.
events.disputed: The rift is described only as talk; the snippet does not confirm it.

events.summary: French output shrank and inflation accelerated, leaving the economy at a standstill, according to a minister. The statement points to a stalled economy.
New Zealand beat India by 87 runs in a T20 match, with Glenn Phillips scoring 107. Reports credit Seifert with guiding New Zealand to the consolation win.
events.disputed: Outlets differ on the match number, calling it the fourth or fifth T20.
events.story: new zealand consolation win india t20

events.summary: German inflation slowed more than expected in October. The economy also grew more than expected in the third quarter, helped by a fuel tax cut.
events.story: german inflation slows october q3 growth

events.summary: Pope Leo XIV became the first pontiff to cast a ballot in a US election, mailing in a ballot for the midterm elections. The Chicago-born pontiff has a tense relationship with Trump.
events.story: pope leo votes us midterm election

events.summary: The US approved a sale of Patriot missiles to Ukraine. The sale is reported as worth $2.1 billion, and the interceptors are described as the only effective weapon against Russia's ballistic missiles.
events.disputed: Outlets report different figures: $2.1 billion in one account and 500 missiles in another.

events.summary: Federal Reserve officials made the case for interest rate hikes amid ongoing inflation concerns. The snippet covers only this headline.
Mexico's economy grew more than forecast in the third quarter, easing pressure for interest rate cuts.
Government data shows the Ebola outbreak in DR Congo has killed more than 5,000 people and infected over 10,000, its deadliest outbreak.
Canadian PM Mark Carney said Canada is seeking closer EU ties to diversify partnerships beyond the Americas, favoring an 'associate membership' concept despite German pushback.
North Korea says sanctions have not denied its status as a nuclear weapons state.
A manhunt is under way after a Toronto real estate CEO and his two daughters were shot and his wife assaulted with a hammer in a home invasion.
The Colombian central bank held its interest rate and will shore up reserves with $2 billion.
Senegal opened Africa's first Youth Olympic Games, marking the first Olympic event held in Africa.
Egypt's foreign minister said it fears an escalation in the Iran war would be more destructive.
BBC Verify went inside an election centre to show how US midterm mail-in ballots are secured and counted.
Donald Trump promised to slash gasoline prices below $2 a gallon in his first year, but gasoline, diesel and jet fuel prices all rose.
Turkey has nominated former foreign minister and UN ambassador Feridun Hadi Sinirlioglu for UN secretary-general, state media reported, with President Erdogan's official backing.
Ethiopia's prime minister has put ministers through military training, a move in line with his previous emphasis on military preparedness.
Stocks started the week strongly but ended lower after Big Tech earnings reignited fears about AI spending, pushing investors into defensive stocks.
events.story: stocks reverse on ai spending fears

events.summary: On Brazil's election day, buses stopped running and supporters known as 'Lula's Army' took over drivers' car keys to help voters get to polls.
Iran's supreme leader Khamenei warned the United States and Israel against new attacks as tensions mount over a possible return to fighting, after Trump and Netanyahu threatened military action.
events.story: iran warns us israel new strikes

events.summary: The US and Canada see growing interest in a limited ceasefire in the Black Sea, according to Reuters.
Creative artists in Grayndler, Albanese's inner Sydney seat, are protesting potential changes to copyright laws proposed in an AI plan, causing discontent for the prime minister.
Ghana says Russia will back a 2,000 MW nuclear power plant and deepen bilateral ties.
The FBI has linked North Korea to the theft of about $6 billion from Binance, described as the biggest hack in history.
A shooting at a Spirit Halloween store in California left a pregnant woman dead and 6 wounded, and a mass shooting after an Alabama football game left 1 dead and 8 wounded.
A judge has dismissed President Trump's lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal over a letter related to Jeffrey Epstein. The AP headline describes the suit as 'grasping at straws'.

Alaska Senate incumbent Dan Sullivan, a Republican seeking re-election, denies knowing about an alleged plot to put a second Dan Sullivan on the ballot. He and allies accuse Democrats of trying to confuse voters.
events.disputed: Plot allegations are contested; the candidate denies knowledge and Democrats are accused by his allies.

events.summary: Finance Minister Katy Gallagher says growing budget pressures mean the government cannot promise overall savings in its December update. Australians face another expected interest rate rise amid high inflation.
Bangladesh has formed a wage board as garment protests have turned violent. Few further details are given in the available text.
Two 16-year-old boys were killed when a stolen car left the road, struck several trees and caught fire in Perth's north-east. Police say the teenagers were the driver and passenger.
events.story: perth teens killed stolen car crash

events.summary: A lobby group says Germany must do more to boost its gas reserves, as storage levels have hit a record low.
Bulgarians are voting in a presidential runoff marked by regional security threats.

The Texas Senate race, described as a $500m contest, may be the most closely watched in the US midterms. Analysis asks whether Democrat Talarico can turn the tide for a party used to heartbreak in Texas.

Thousands, and by some reports tens of thousands, joined a New Delhi rally called by opposition leader Rahul Gandhi. Protesters demand the resignation of the chief election commissioner amid tight security.
events.story: india opposition rally election chief resignation

events.summary: Binance, the world's biggest crypto exchange, said it would resume withdrawals after a suspension caused by a major hack. The FBI has tied the hack to North Korea, and Binance said it covered 95% of the $6.3 billion in stolen tokens.
events.story: binance hack north korea withdrawals resume

events.summary: A driver has been charged after a pedestrian died at the scene of a crash at Salisbury North in Adelaide's north, SA Police said. The crash happened at about 10am on Sunday.
Donald Trump has lost allies after elections in Serbia and Brazil, where Flavio Bolsonaro failed to gain power and Aleksandar Vucic was voted out. Trump has claimed electoral fraud.
events.disputed: Trump's electoral fraud claim is presented as his assertion and is not verified in the snippets.
events.story: trump allies lose serbia brazil elections

events.summary: Emergency response teams from some of WA's biggest mines competed hundreds of metres underground in the annual mine rescue competition, the biggest in a decade.

A third weekend of youth-led rallies has spread across Europe, from France to Portugal, Italy and Germany. Tens of thousands demonstrated in Germany's biggest cities to demand better education and lower living costs.
Senegal hosts the Youth Olympic Games, the first Olympic event on the African continent, opened by Senegal's president in Dakar. 136 Senegalese athletes are competing, supported by 6,000 volunteers.
Jamaal Bowman says he would be in Congress had he kept quiet, in an interview with Marc Lamont Hill about the battle between progressives and the Democratic establishment.
events.story: jamaal bowman progressives democratic establishment battle

events.summary: Mediators continue US-Iran negotiations amid war rhetoric. Trump says the latest talks are going fine, while Iranian leaders say they favour diplomacy but are ready to respond to US attacks.
events.disputed: Trump's claim that talks are going fine is his own characterisation and is not independently confirmed in the snippets.

events.summary: Senegal celebrated as the Youth Olympic Games got underway in Dakar, the first Olympic competition held on African soil. An opening ceremony was attended by 30,000 people.
Democratic wins in Congress would shift the trade debate but would fall short of rolling back US tariffs, according to Reuters.
events.story: democratic wins congress tariff trade debate

events.summary: A France 24 photo roundup of the past week covers Lula's reelection in Brazil, razor-sharp margins in the Israeli general elections, and a deadly high-speed train collision in Spain.
events.story: week in pictures lula israel spain

events.summary: Thousands rallied in New Delhi demanding India's election chief resign, with hundreds of police, some carrying batons and shields, deployed around the site.
Russia opened a terrorism case over a drone attack on a Ukrainian-named major Russian oil refinery, which reportedly sustained significant damage.
events.disputed: Damage and attack claims are reported by Ukraine and attributed to reports; not independently confirmed in the snippets.
events.story: russia terrorism case refinery drone attack

events.summary: South Africa's Lions rugby team returned home after a traumatic Europe tour.
China's BYD extended its sales growth streak, supported by strong exports.
The Trump White House is mapping a path to govern without Congress if Democrats win the midterm elections.
events.disputed: Plans are reported only as mapped paths; the snippets give no details of implementation.

events.summary: A fire broke out at a hotel in Dingboche, Nepal, along the popular trekking route to Mount Everest Base Camp.
Analysis says the 2026 midterm election could affect municipal bonds through state tax measures, new bond supply and the makeup of Congress.
CNBC highlights top Wall Street analysts' bullish long-term picks for three stocks, backed by research.
Companies including Santander and Novartis say AI is beginning to boost revenue, cut costs or improve profitability as investors seek returns.
Violence at French protests eased while scattered riots hit Germany ahead of more planned action.
Australian house prices have fallen for seven consecutive months, with the pace of decline the fastest in 40 years, according to a property research group.
Iran says it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz in a shorter period if conditions are met, while Trump says the US still has targets to take care of as diplomacy is explored.
Palestinians in Lebanon, one of the country's most vulnerable communities, are struggling to make ends meet as high energy prices and inflation worsen their situation.
Russian strikes cut power to thousands of people in Ukraine, while drones damaged a Russian facility.
Israeli attacks across the Gaza Strip killed at least eight to nine Palestinians, including a four-year-old, according to Al Jazeera reports on Sunday strikes in Gaza City and Khan Younis.
events.disputed: Reports differ on the death toll, given as at least eight and at least nine.

events.summary: Poland's constitutional crisis deepened as the European Commission urged President Karol Nawrocki to recognise new judges appointed by Prime Minister Donald Tusk, ahead of next year's parliamentary election.
Iran and Qatari mediators held a third day of talks aimed at ending the US-Iran war.
The Northern Territory government is accused of moving to scrap a legal requirement to set aside water for the environment, which a green group called an extreme attack on nature.
events.disputed: The green group's characterisation of the move as blatant and shameless is an opinion from one side.

events.summary: King Charles III will deliver a speech on slavery to the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua on Tuesday, concluding his nine-day Caribbean tour.
President Herzog must nominate a candidate to form a new Israeli government by November 11, with fraught negotiations likely to follow.
Morocco is celebrating after a UN resolution on Western Sahara was defeated, as the mandate for the UN mission that monitors the 1991 truce and planned referendum in the disputed territory expires.
Senate races in November may help determine the fate of Social Security, as its retirement trust fund may run out in 2032, and senators elected then will be in office when that deadline arrives.

A French student union leader said high school blockades across France will restart on Monday, as President Emmanuel Macron has called for classes to resume after new government measures on the ongoing education crisis.
events.story: france high school blockades education crisis

events.summary: South Africa's Nortje is in contention for a test return against Australia after a long absence, while Green is ruled out of the first test and Rabada is in contention. AP reports South Africa has a player expected to step up if Rabada cannot play.
events.story: south africa australia first test squad

events.summary: Voting took place in Brazil's presidential election, where Lula faces Trump ally Flávio Bolsonaro. Reuters reports Trump's remarks on the election suggest Lula is isolated, according to Bolsonaro.
Brazil's presidential election heads to a runoff, with Bolsonaro and Lula advancing to a second round. Both candidates and supporters reacted to the first-round result.
Polls closed in Brazil's first-round presidential vote, with Lula ahead in polls and a runoff considered likely. Brazil's benchmark stock index soared as Bolsonaro topped the first-round vote.

The South African rand moved within a narrow range, pressured at times by a stronger dollar and a local fuel price hike, and steadied after weak manufacturing data. Middle East conflict and US inflation were cited as factors for sentiment.
Thailand is preparing to host the IMF-World Bank meetings in Bangkok amid forecast rain. Reuters reported exclusively that US Treasury Secretary Bessent will skip the meetings.
Tropical Storm Simon formed in the Pacific Ocean off Mexico's southwestern coast and strengthened into a hurricane. Reuters reports it threatens a tourist region.
Kenya's central bank held its key rate and said inflation is within target despite a recent rise.
Fed minutes indicate another interest rate hike is likely this year to combat persistent inflation.
Trump says the US will not resume military strikes on Iran or attack Iran before the November 3 midterm elections.
Brazil's Flavio Bolsonaro vows to keep pension increases above the inflation rate.
South African-born jurist and former ICC judge Navi Pillay has won the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for her work in international justice.
Houthi strikes on Riyadh airport killed three Saudis as the war escalates.
A Houthi strike on a Saudi airport killed 12 people, the worst attack on the kingdom in a decade, and a new attack a day later killed one more.
India's inflation rose to 5.54% in September, strengthening the case for further interest rate hikes.
Japan's wholesale inflation remains elevated, keeping alive the view that the Bank of Japan will raise rates.
Iran says a ship sank after striking a mine in the Strait of Hormuz, and masked settlers attacked European diplomats in the occupied West Bank.

Nigeria's inflation rate eased slightly but remains a worry for many citizens.

New Zealand's third-quarter inflation slowed to 3.7%, but expectations remain for a rate hike next week.
events.story: new zealand inflation slows hike expected

Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado returned to Venezuela to a welcome from supporters, as the US proposed elections in Venezuela for 2027, Machado said.
Flavio Bolsonaro said Brazil federal police asked for his passports and he missed a deadline to surrender them; Trump said he approves of him coming to the US.

Jordan carried out a deadly strike in Syria in retaliation for a church attack; the strike on a village killed five people, including women and children, Syrian health officials said.
Flavio Bolsonaro left Brazil for the US after his election defeat, a source and media said; the State Department said he and his family will get US visas.

events.summary: Thousands rallied outside Portugal's parliament over the housing crisis, and police cleared a new Lisbon housing protest camp.

The RBA has primed markets for an interest rate rise. A central bank forecast that unemployment may need to rise further shows it cares more about inflation than full employment, columnist Greg Jericho writes.
Ethiopia says it received Russian Su-35 jets and S-400 air defence systems. The acquisition comes amid ongoing fighting in the northern Tigray region.
Putin is seeking to expand ties with African countries at a Russia-Africa summit held in Moscow.
The US has imposed sanctions on Rwanda's defence ministry over its involvement in the eastern Congo conflict.
Canadian Prime Minister Carney reports progress in trade talks with Trump days before US midterms, though Reuters describes the progress as limited.

The death toll from the Spanish train crash has risen to 69 as the search for victims continues.
With more than 90% of votes counted, Israel's election appears deadlocked. The most likely outcome may be new elections, according to BBC scenarios.

ECB President Christine Lagarde will step down several months early to have more freedom to speak on matters that are not monetary policy, fuelling speculation about her future plans.

China's central bank is stepping up its shift toward the overnight rate as its main policy anchor.

A manhunt is underway after a Toronto real estate CEO and his two daughters were shot and his wife assaulted with a hammer in a home invasion.
The Colombia central bank held its policy rate and will shore up reserves with $2 billion.
Starved residents evacuated from Russian-occupied Oleshky reached Ukrainian-held territory during a rare local ceasefire, describing isolation, food shortages and shelling.
Egypt's foreign minister said he fears an escalation in the Iran war would be more destructive.
BBC Verify looks behind the scenes at how mail-in ballots for the US midterm elections are processed, secured and counted.
Virgin Media O2 is set to cut thousands of jobs, with the number of roles not yet finalised, according to Sky News and the BBC.

events.summary: Gasoline, diesel and jet fuel prices all rose despite Donald Trump's promise to slash energy costs and gasoline prices below $2 a gallon.
Ethiopia's prime minister has put ministers through military training, consistent with his emphasis on military preparedness.
Reuters reports that during a bus stoppage on Brazil's election day, supporters known as 'Lula's Army' took drivers' car keys. Details beyond the headline are not in the snippet.
Ghana says Russia will back a 2,000 MW nuclear power plant and deepen bilateral ties.

A US judge dismissed President Donald Trump's US$10 billion defamation suit against the Wall Street Journal and Rupert Murdoch over a birthday letter to Jeffrey Epstein, with prejudice so it cannot be refiled. Trump denied writing the letter.

events.summary: The Youth Olympic Games opened in Senegal, marking the first Olympic event held on the African continent.
Thousands gathered in central Delhi at a mega rally by India's opposition calling for the chief election commissioner to resign.

A weekly photo review covering Lula's reelection in Brazil, razor-sharp margins in Israeli general elections, and a deadly high-speed train collision in Spain.
A parish in Uruguay struggling with violence is preparing for a visit by Pope Leo XIV.
Taiwan accuses China of harassment after a standoff between coast guard ships.
Analysis says the 2026 midterm election could affect municipal bonds through state tax measures, new bond supply and the makeup of Congress.
A CNBC piece highlights three stocks that top Wall Street analysts are bullish on for the long term.
Companies including Santander and Novartis say AI is beginning to boost revenue, cut costs or improve profitability, according to earnings reports.
The longest truce of the war in Ukraine, in the Kherson region, ended Sunday after Russia refused to extend the ceasefire that had enabled a humanitarian mission.
Portugal is weighing a bigger stake in Galp after the collapse of the Moeve merger, a minister said.
Poland's constitutional crisis deepened as the European Commission urged President Karol Nawrocki to recognise judges appointed by Prime Minister Donald Tusk, ahead of next year's election.
Qatar's market surged while Gulf markets slid over concerns about the Iran war.
A student union leader said high school blockades across France will restart Monday, after the government announced new measures to address the education crisis.
Iran and Qatari mediators held a third day of talks aimed at ending the US-Iran war.
Russia's FSB says it detained a minor suspected of planning an attack at a Moscow park, after a US tip-off.

events.summary: Markets expect oil to keep rising while Treasury yields have declined. A warning suggests traders and investors may be more worried about an AI crash than inflation.
events.story: oil ai bond market trades shift

events.summary: Donald Trump held rallies in Iowa and Kansas as Republicans work to keep control of the Senate and House. He returned to the campaign trail after a break at Mar-a-Lago in Florida.
Protesters in New Delhi carried a one-kilometre banner bearing the names of people removed from India's voter rolls.
Dozens of garment workers clashed with police in Dhaka, Bangladesh, in protests over low pay.
events.story: bangladesh garment workers low pay protest

events.summary: Israeli strikes in Gaza killed at least eight Palestinians, including five Hamas-run police officers and a child, according to medics and officials in two separate attacks.
Pacific scholars and security experts warn that growing US-China military competition must not come at the expense of the people of Micronesia.
Exit polls suggest acting President Iliana Iotova wins Bulgaria's presidential runoff, which would make her the nation's first elected female president if results confirm it on Monday.
events.disputed: Based on exit polls; results not yet confirmed.

events.summary: Residents of Oleshky who requested evacuation were reunited with loved ones in Ukraine on Saturday, October 31, during the first humanitarian truce of the war. The city is under Russian occupation.
India's opposition parties staged major protests in New Delhi on Sunday against Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government and a nationwide voter list review.
Police started armed patrols in Sydney in response to last year's deadly shooting at a Hanukkah festival at Bondi Beach. The new unit is a security measure.
Reuters reports the Trump White House is mapping a path to govern without Congress if Democrats win the midterms. Snippet is headline-only, so details are limited.

A US judge dismissed a Trump-linked election lawsuit in Alaska brought by the Justice Department. Senator Sullivan pledged to honour the Alaska race outcome, contrasting with the administration's challenge to the state's certification.
Haley Stevens, who lost the Michigan Democratic Senate primary to Abdul El-Sayed, endorsed Republican opponent days before the vote, causing a party spat.
The AP college football poll shows Ohio State falling out of the top 10, UCLA moving into the top 5, and New Mexico earning its first-ever AP ranking.
Al Jazeera asks how the Iran war will shape the US midterm vote, noting the conflict has become a central issue ahead of Tuesday's polls.
Canadian PM Carney said he had a good conversation with Trump on trade. Snippets give no further details of the talks.
Arsenal won at Anfield for the first time since 2012 to go top, three points clear of Man City, in a match marred by VAR drama over a missed Liverpool penalty shout.
events.disputed: Snippets describe the VAR penalty decision as a missed clear penalty; this is one outlet's characterization.

events.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog called for calm as mediations begin between parties to form a new government after an election that failed to produce a majority.
Video shows a house collapsing into a swollen river in Ecuador, where torrential rains and floods linked to El Nino have struck.
Haley Stevens, defeated in the Michigan Democratic Senate primary, broke ranks to endorse the Republican nominee days before Tuesday's midterm vote.
Fiji's coalition government is reportedly falling apart ahead of the crucial third reading of a bill to change the 2013 Constitution, putting Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka under pressure.

Russian strikes cut power to thousands of people in Ukraine, while drones reportedly damaged a Russian facility. A rare humanitarian ceasefire had earlier let civilians evacuate the occupied city of Oleshky.

Donald Trump is campaigning for embattled Senate seats after a Halloween party at Mar-a-Lago. Judges in Alaska and California threw out lawsuits from his administration aimed at blocking election results.
Homeowners in north Queensland are struggling to obtain or afford insurance almost two years after the floods.
Nationals leader Matt Canavan will run for a Queensland lower house seat, setting up a possible contest with One Nation's James Ashby. Michelle Landry will not recontest the seat of Capricornia.
The husband of a woman killed by a bus has called for tougher driving tests for older drivers. The 72-year-old bus driver later admitted a charge of careless driving causing death.
Victoria Police are investigating several crashes on the state's roads over Melbourne Cup weekend that left eight people dead and others fighting for life.
Pasifika voters in Aotearoa say the election is about basics such as affordable food, petrol and health services, rejecting handouts.
Former French Prime Minister Édouard Philippe ruled out competing in a centre-right primary, rejecting a proposal from rival Gabriel Attal to select a single candidate by vote.
US officials say a small business jet crashed into a neighbourhood in southern Florida, killing all nine people aboard.

South Africa's Nortje is eyeing a test return against Australia after a lengthy absence, while Australia's Green has been ruled out of the first test. Rabada is in contention to play, with South Africa reportedly trusting someone to step up if he cannot.
events.story: south africa australia first test squad

events.summary: Lula is reported ahead in polls for Brazil's first-round presidential vote, and both Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro have wrapped up campaigns. Reports say the race is heading to a runoff.
India is seen kicking off a rate hike cycle as inflation broadens and peer central banks turn hawkish.
Spain's prime minister has called a snap election, aiming to seize momentum over the housing crisis.
The South African rand has been moving with the dollar, fuel price hikes, weak metals, weak manufacturing data and Middle East conflict and US inflation sentiment.
Thailand is preparing to host the IMF-World Bank meetings in Bangkok, with forecast rain, while a Reuters exclusive reports US Treasury Secretary Bessent will skip them.
Tropical Storm Simon formed in the Pacific off Mexico's southwestern coast and strengthened into a hurricane, threatening the tourist region.
Kenya's central bank held its key rate and sees inflation within target despite a recent rise.
Brazil's Flavio Bolsonaro vows to keep pension increases above the inflation rate.
Trump says the US will not resume military strikes on Iran or attack Iran before the November 3 midterm elections.
A Houthi strike on a Saudi airport killed 12, reported as the worst attack on the kingdom in a decade. A later attack on the airport killed one, a day after a strike killed 13.
Australia beat New Zealand 24-22 in the Rugby League World Cup opener, with Bostock scoring three tries. New Zealand fullback Ponga suffered a broken arm in the match.
Japan's wholesale inflation remains elevated, keeping alive the Bank of Japan's view that a rate hike may be considered.
India's inflation rose to 5.54% in September, strengthening the case for further rate hikes.
Iran says a ship sank after striking a mine in the Strait of Hormuz and has increased threats to shipping. Masked settlers attacked European diplomats in the occupied West Bank.
Flavio Bolsonaro slightly leads Lula ahead of the Brazil runoff, according to a Quaest poll, though Datafolha and other polls show his lead narrowing. Corruption is a top voter concern.
events.disputed: Snippets report conflicting poll results on the runoff lead.

events.summary: US inflation heated up in September, putting a Fed rate hike this month back on the table, according to reporting.
Nasdaq ended sharply lower as hot inflation data stirred rate-hike worries among investors.
French glassmaker Duralex has been pulled back from the brink for the fifth time in 25 years by an entrepreneur promising an environmentally conscious new chapter.
Nigeria's inflation rate eased slightly but remains a worry for many citizens.
A gold mine collapse in southwest Colombia has killed at least 14 people and injured 7, according to Reuters and AP reports. The death toll was initially reported as at least 6.
Nigeria has recorded its first Ebola case as the outbreak reaches West Africa, and the Africa CDC is calling an Ebola crisis summit.
The death toll from a Houthi attack on a Yemen training camp has risen to 73, according to Reuters.
New Zealand third-quarter inflation slowed to 3.7%, but expectations remain for a rate hike next week.
events.story: new zealand inflation slows hike expected

events.summary: A magnitude 7.2 earthquake struck waters near Vanuatu, according to the USGS as reported by Reuters.
Gunmen killed at least 40 people in northeastern Nigeria, according to Amnesty International via Reuters. AP reports at least 62 people were killed in an attack on a community in the same region.
events.disputed: The death toll differs between sources: at least 40 (Reuters, citing Amnesty) and at least 62 (AP).

events.summary: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has won Brazil's election and vowed to govern for all. Jair Bolsonaro contests the loss while Donald Trump says the election looked rigged, without citing evidence.
events.disputed: Trump's claim that the election looked rigged is made without citing evidence; Bolsonaro contests the loss.

events.summary: Flavio Bolsonaro says Brazil federal police asked for his passports and missed a deadline to surrender them. After landing in the US, he declared himself Brazil's rightful leader, and Trump said he approves of him coming to the US.
events.disputed: Flavio Bolsonaro's claim to be Brazil's rightful leader is contested in the snippets.

events.summary: Global leaders have congratulated Brazil President Lula on his reelection, according to AP and Reuters.
Jordan carried out a deadly strike in Syria in retaliation for a church attack. The strike killed five people, including women and children, Syrian health officials said.
Trump and Rubio plan to visit an oil tanker in Texas carrying the first Venezuelan crude under a deal Trump touted as record. Reports say reality is now setting in for the deal.
Brazil's Flavio Bolsonaro left Brazil for the US after losing the election, according to a source and media reports. The State Department says he and his family will get US visas.
Zambia's president appointed a new mines minister in cabinet changes following the election.
The RBA has signalled an interest rate rise, and a central bank forecast suggests unemployment may need to rise further, showing it prioritises inflation over full employment.
Ethiopia says it received Russian Su-35 jets, with S-400 air defence systems to follow, amid ongoing fighting in northern Tigray.
Putin met African leaders at a Moscow Russia-Africa summit aimed at expanding Russia's ties with African countries.
At least 68 people died in Spain's second major train crash this year. The minister has refused to resign over it.
The death toll from the Spanish train crash has risen to 69 as the search for victims continues.
With more than 90% of votes counted, Israel's election appears deadlocked, and new elections may be the most likely outcome.
Uganda says 27 of its citizens were killed or presumed dead while fighting for Russia in Ukraine.
EU chief von der Leyen continues calling Canada an 'associate member' in a partnership vision laid out at a Montreal summit, despite opposition from some member states including Germany.
events.disputed: Some EU members, including Germany, reportedly oppose the 'associate member' term.

events.summary: Egypt's central bank raised interest rates for the first time since March 2024.
ECB President Christine Lagarde will step down several months early to have more freedom to engage on non-monetary policy matters, fueling speculation about her future plans.
The US has proposed Venezuela elections for 2027, according to opposition leader María Machado, who called for elections after returning from nearly a year in exile.
events.disputed: The US proposal timing is reported via Machado's statement; details are limited in the snippets.

events.summary: Dockworkers at more than 100 ports worldwide, in Europe and beyond, struck against arms shipments and war deaths.
US Democrats face an identity crisis and tough questions about what the party stands for and who should represent it, regardless of midterm election results.

China says a stealth attack drone made its first takeoff and landing on an amphibious ship.
Federal Reserve officials made the case for rate hikes amid ongoing inflation concerns.
Mexico's economy beat forecasts in the third quarter, reducing pressure for rate cuts.
Iran's IRGC Navy said tankers caught fire and then that two tankers exploded after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz.

events.disputed: The strikes are described as 'defensive' by officials; the characterization is unverified.

events.summary: Oil prices rose as Iran said a war deal remains distant, with reports of a US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island.
Financial leaders say big-ticket tech deals need to keep pace with the AI boom, but risks remain high.
A US official says the US has conducted defensive strikes on Iranian targets in the Strait of Hormuz.
The Reserve Bank of Australia raised its cash rate to 4.85 percent, and inflation is expected to stay above 3 percent over the coming year.
US voters head to the polls on election day to elect members of the House of Representatives and Senate, with control of Congress at stake.
Singapore's minister says it will push for stronger action against transboundary haze when it chairs ASEAN in 2027.
Rising interest rates and inflation are squeezing household budgets ahead of Christmas, with disposable incomes eaten into.
Researchers have detected signals from the smallest distances ever probed.
One person died at the scene of a serious crash that closed a Southland highway, police confirmed.
A controversial 155-turbine wind farm in Victoria's north was approved one day before the state government enters caretaker mode, blindsiding local farmers.
Beth Jenkins says her cancer was initially missed after being told she was too young to have the disease, and it had spread by the time she was diagnosed.
The Asian Football Confederation has postponed the 2027 Asian Cup until late 2027 because of conflict in the Middle East, with reports citing attacks on Saudi Arabia.
events.story: asian cup postponed middle east conflict

events.summary: AI data centres could undermine the UK's emissions goals, according to BBC News reporting.
Treasurer Jim Chalmers says he will be helpful on inflation but rejects blame for a widely expected interest rate hike, pointing to weak public demand figures.
One Indian national was killed in an attack on a ship near Oman, according to the Indian foreign ministry.
India faces prolonged food inflation affecting grains, chicken and milk, according to Reuters.
Pop star James Blunt discusses new music, appearing on The Traitors, and his attempt to be banished from the show during James Acaster's banishment.
Heavy rain has fallen in eastern India following a second cyclone in a week.
Children's author Craig Silvey published a 9,000-word apology after his sentencing for child sex offences, as he begins a seven-month sentence for possessing child exploitation material.
events.disputed: Child protection organisations say the apology is more about him than the victims.

events.summary: A court heard that Beau Lamarre-Condon cried and claimed to have PTSD in a police interview after the deaths of Jesse Baird and Luke Davies, and asked police not to judge him.
Polls suggest Democrats could take control of US Congress in this week's midterm elections, but experts warn the outcome may not be so straightforward.
events.disputed: Experts warn polling predictions may be wrong; outcome uncertain.

events.summary: Early feedback on a pilot community mental health hub in Cumbria is reported as positive.
Drax and Brookfield are partnering on a $27 billion AI data centre in the UK.
events.story: drax brookfield uk ai data centre

events.summary: A psychiatrist has left New Zealand's public health system after a patient at Hillmorton Hospital, Zakariye Mohamed Hussein, was linked to the stabbing death of Laisa Waka Tunidau in June 2022.

Ahead of Tuesday's RBA decision, a fifth rate hike is expected to add pressure on households, with voters frustrated and Labor's political luck in question as Pauline Hanson and Angus Taylor may benefit.
The BBC has published a guide on how to follow the US midterm elections across TV, radio and online.
Uganda has arrested former army deputy chief Elwelu, who was stripped of his military rank; a military spokesman says 15 guns were recovered in his possession.
LPG prices in Pakistan have soared, forcing rickshaw drivers to cut back on meals.

Australia says easing of visa rules has led to a surge in British visitor numbers, putting pressure on the local workforce, and Prime Minister Anthony Albanese is looking at changing the rules for British workers.
An Indian national was killed and a New Zealander injured when two helicopters, one carrying tourists and one cargo, collided while landing near Mount Everest's South Base Camp.
Displaced Sudanese are returning to Khartoum, one of the areas hit earliest and hardest by the war between the SAF and RSF, facing new challenges.
Apple shares slid as higher memory costs raised concerns about its profit margins.
Beaconsfield mine collapse survivor Todd Russell is leaving hospital treatment to spend his remaining days at home with family amid a health battle.
Two people died in a plane crash; the wreckage was found in a remote search area south of Castor Peak near Nelson.
Americans are voting in midterm elections that will shape Congress for the final years of Trump's presidency and test politics without him.
Air pollution has spiked in Lahore and Delhi, with both cities choking in smog.
China's foreign minister met Southeast Asian officials as Beijing pushes to strengthen relations.
events.story: china foreign minister southeast asia meeting

events.summary: A new African credit rating agency is in talks with 15 sovereign borrowers.
events.story: new africa credit rating agency talks

events.summary: Polls have opened in closely contested US midterm elections, with Democrats eyeing historic gains in Congress; results could take days and markets may react.
Saudi Aramco's third-quarter net profit rose 34% to $36.25 billion despite Houthi attacks on its infrastructure and headquarters, helped by elevated oil prices.
Lebanon has cut power to public bodies as its electricity crisis deepens, with political disputes and war worsening the situation. Experts say deeper reforms are needed.
Republican Ashley Hinson and Democrat Josh Turek are making their final campaign appeals in Iowa's Senate race ahead of the midterm elections.
South Africa's diesel price will drop while petrol prices are little changed after a levy cut.
events.story: south africa fuel price levy cut

events.summary: France, Germany and Italy face a volatile bond market as war inflation bites, and US tech giants issuing billions in AI bonds may compete with European governments and raise borrowing costs.
events.story: ai giants bonds european borrowing costs

events.summary: Sudan demands UN accountability after deadly RSF drone attacks, which have exposed deep divisions between Sudan and Ethiopia in a complex regional crisis.
Schaeffler will cut 3,460 jobs and shut five European plants as the auto industry slump bites.
Spanish authorities confirmed two Australians are among the dead after two high-speed trains crashed in Spain.
The US has carried out a series of 'defensive strikes' on Iranian locations near Hormuz, with explosions heard on Qeshm.
The US has attacked Qeshm Island for the first time since June, while Iran's president Pezeshkian signals more diplomacy as Iran and the US pursue parallel tracks toward peace and war.
Attackers ambushed police in Nigeria's Zamfara state, killing at least eight people, officials say.
The US reportedly attacked Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz as President Trump signaled progress in negotiations with Tehran to end the eight-month-old conflict.
events.disputed: The attack is reported by the Wall Street Journal citing unnamed US officials.

events.summary: A press review from Poland covers the standoff between Prime Minister Donald Tusk and the nationalist president over the composition of the constitutional court, alongside a report on cheese theft in Europe.
An EU court adviser says Google's AI chatbot use of press items may infringe copyright rules.
events.disputed: This is a non-binding opinion from an EU court adviser, not a final ruling.

events.summary: A Russian strike on a humanitarian aid site in southern Ukraine has killed at least 31 people with dozens still missing, amid overnight strikes on power plants and hospitals across the country.
Prediction markets face a test in the US midterm elections as election betting grows, with questions about how accurate such markets are on elections.
events.disputed: The accuracy of prediction markets on elections is questioned and not settled.

events.summary: Alaska Senate candidates are trading accusations ahead of the election.
events.disputed: The accusations between candidates are not detailed in the available text.

events.summary: Apple says it is unsure when it will get more foldable iPhones ahead of Christmas, admitting constraints are affecting supplies of the iPhone Duo despite strong sales.
A report finds Britons have become less engaged with their jobs and less willing to put in extra effort, which could be hitting the economy.
DR Congo opposition leader Prince Epenge has been arrested and transferred to prison on charges of spreading fake news.
events.disputed: The charges of spreading fake news against Epenge are not verified in the snippet.

events.summary: Apple's margin outlook is pressuring tech stocks as a reported US strike lifts oil prices, with midterm voting underway amid market volatility.
China's military vice chair met Russia's defence minister in Beijing.
events.story: china russia military vice chair meeting

events.summary: Uganda announced it has begun withdrawing its troops from Somalia, where it was the first country to deploy to help Mogadishu under the African Union mission against al-Shabab rebels.
An Indian tourist was killed after two helicopters collided near Everest base camp; the aircraft crashed just metres from the ground while trying to land at the same spot.
Students blockaded dozens of French high schools on Tuesday to pressure the government over education reforms, as unions prepared a nationwide strike later in the week.
The UK and EU agreed a draft deal to scrap Brexit red tape on food exports, the most significant part of the so-called Brexit reset so far, ahead of a UK-EU summit later this month.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio urged Venezuela to release remaining political prisoners and discussed laying groundwork for free, fair and credible elections.
events.story: us urges venezuela free political prisoners

events.summary: Renewed strikes on Black Sea shipping threaten grain exports, drive up food prices and deepen global food insecurity, according to Al Jazeera.
events.story: black sea attacks grain food supply

events.summary: Four people were charged with attempted murder after South African farmer Donovan Marx, 50, was shot and tortured; right-wing groups claim a genocide of white people, a claim widely discredited.
events.disputed: Right-wing groups' claim of genocide against white people is widely discredited.

events.summary: Released Al Jazeera Arabic correspondent Montaser Nassar described how Israeli forces raided his home and arrested him.
Brazilian economists raised their inflation and interest rate forecasts after Lula's reelection.
Two police officers guarding polio workers in Pakistan were shot dead by attackers on a motorcycle who opened fire on their police car in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.
Senegal's opposition-dominated parliament, led by Pastef and Ousmane Sonko, rejected a revised budget bill on Tuesday, leaving the new IMF bailout programme in doubt.
Andrew Scott's drama Elsinore leads the nominations for the British independent film awards.
Investors are preparing for a possible shake-up in Congress as Election Day arrives.
CNBC's Santoli argues the AI-driven bull market likely needs tech stocks to recover in order to keep advancing.
events.story: ai bull market needs tech stocks

events.summary: Ferrari raised its 2026 guidance on Tuesday after third-quarter revenue and adjusted earnings per share edged past Wall Street expectations.
Brazil has published what it describes as the first global roadmap for phasing out fossil fuels.
Qatar's foreign ministry spokesperson Majed al-Ansari says regional neighbours and international partners are working toward a US-Iran deal and Qatar remains hopeful.
Brazil concluded COP30 with fossil fuel and forest roadmaps, urging a shift from talks to action.
The Saudi Pro League has postponed matches after the Asian Cup was rescheduled, citing additional flexibility in the domestic football calendar.
An Iranian commander set out five conditions for regional security. Mediator Qatar says the US and Iran are studying proposals to resume negotiations and it is hopeful of an agreement.
events.story: iran us negotiations resume qatar mediation

events.summary: Officials say at least nine 3,000kg aerial bombs hit a southern Ukrainian village, killing 31 people at an aid centre. The president called the attack utterly horrific.
Trump says the US will stop paying $4 billion in military aid to Israel after the end of 2026.
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Poland prevented an attempted provocation on its border with the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad overnight, giving few details.
events.disputed: Few details were given about the alleged provocation.

events.summary: Californians are voting on a ballot initiative for a one-time tax on billionaires to fund the state's healthcare system. Global oil prices fell sharply on the eve of the US midterm elections.
US crude oil fell below $95 per barrel as markets hope for a diplomatic resolution to the Iran war, after the US and Iranian presidents signalled openness to a diplomatic solution.
events.story: oil prices fall iran diplomacy hopes

events.summary: Thailand is hosting IMF-World Bank meetings in Bangkok, with Middle East war and high debt levels expected to dominate; rain is forecast and a debt rework guide was issued ahead of the talks.
Australia's Green has been ruled out of the first test against South Africa, while Rabada is in contention to play. South Africa has a backup plan if Rabada cannot face Australia.
events.story: australia south africa first test cricket

events.summary: The South African rand has held steady amid a stronger dollar, weak metals, weak manufacturing data, Middle East conflict and upcoming US inflation data.
Trump ordered a firing squad for the gunman who killed 13 people at Fort Hood, Texas, and the Pentagon says the Army execution will be livestreamed, a move under legal examination.
events.disputed: Legality of livestreaming the execution is questioned in an explainer.
events.story: fort hood shooter firing squad execution

events.summary: Gulf oil flows rose to an average of 81% of pre-war rate in September, according to data.
Israeli strikes killed people in Gaza, with medics reporting counts of two and five in separate reports.

events.story: navi pillay nobel peace prize sanctions

events.summary: Russia says a plague institute worker's death does not risk an epidemic, and the CDC sees low plague risk while monitoring arrivals from Siberia.

events.summary: Bulgaria's president blames Russia's war in Ukraine for a worsening security environment in the Black Sea.
Trump said the US will not resume military strikes on Iran before the Nov. 3 midterm elections.
Outlets AP and Reuters published explainers on the Senate races that will shape control of the US Senate in the 2026 midterm elections.

Brazil's election is set to reshape trade with the United States, with tariffs and minerals at stake.
Attacks on Riyadh airport, attributed to Houthi strikes as the war escalates, killed Saudi nationals, with Saudi authorities reporting more than 300 people hurt in the latest attack.
events.disputed: Reported death tolls differ across outlets, from three to 12.

events.summary: President Trump said Russia will supply diesel to US and global markets, prompting US Republicans and Democrats to urge him to reverse course on the deal.
A Houthi strike on a Saudi airport killed 12, the worst attack on the kingdom in a decade, and a new attack a day later killed one more person.
events.disputed: Reported death tolls differ across outlets, from 12 to 13.

events.summary: Hurricane Simon strengthened to Category 4 off Mexico's Pacific coast and threatens the tourist region.
Hackers heated French supermarket fridges, sparking fires and spoiling food.
Iran has increased the threat to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, alongside other Middle East developments.
events.story: iran strait of hormuz shipping threat

events.summary: French glassmaker Duralex has been rescued from collapse for the fifth time in 25 years by an entrepreneur who vows an environmentally conscious new chapter.
Global stock markets were flat as concerns about AI and interest rates weighed on technology shares.
Brazil's electoral court ruled in Lula's challenge against Meta over alleged pro-Bolsonaro algorithm bias; Meta denies anti-Lula bias and says it treats both campaigns equally ahead of Sunday's vote.

events.summary: South African president reinstated a suspended police chief, who will return to work after the suspension was lifted.
Chile's pension funds reportedly requested curbs on interest-rate bets before they suffered losses, according to Bloomberg.
events.disputed: Report attributed to Bloomberg; not independently confirmed in the snippet.

events.summary: The IMF expects at least one more 25 basis point interest rate hike by the European Central Bank in 2026.
Restaurants that took low-interest pandemic loans during Covid-19 are struggling to repay them, as the industry never recovered enough to cover the debt.

Reuters published an explainer on what to know about the 2026 US midterm elections.
South Africa and Mozambique honored Samora Machel 40 years after his death in a plane crash.
Protesters targeted Meta over alleged election interference and bias in Brazil's presidential runoff campaign.
events.disputed: Interference and bias are described as alleged, not confirmed.

events.summary: A collapse at an illegal gold mine in southwest Colombia killed at least 14 people and injured 7, according to reports; earlier tolls were lower.
An Australian lawmaker lost a leg after being rammed twice in a vehicle attack; a terrorism squad is investigating and the prime minister called it no accident.
Canada's annual inflation rate rose to 3.1% in September.
Morocco's first female prime minister, Fatima El Mansouri, faces religious and political constraints as she considers advancing women's rights.
Phone theft in Brazil has become a key issue in the election campaign.
Australian AI data centre operator NextDC saw shares fall about 40-42% after a revenue delay and cut earnings forecast, with future plans on hold.
A Sudanese drone attack on a market in Abyei killed more than 150 people, according to an official.
events.disputed: Casualty figure is attributed to an official and not independently confirmed in the snippet.

events.summary: An Australian central banker said the inflation outlook is worse and is unsure about a November rate hike.
Nigeria reported its first Ebola case as the outbreak reached West Africa, prompting the Africa CDC to call a crisis summit and urge preparedness.
South Africa storm back to beat Australia by an innings, levelling the test series 1-1. Earlier reports said Australia were following on and South Africa needed six wickets.
events.story: south africa australia test cricket series

events.summary: Elon Musk floated a possible merger of SpaceX and Tesla as SpaceX reported strong quarterly earnings. Coverage also mentions OpenAI revealing more agent misbehaviour amid market turmoil hitting data centre companies.
Stock price listing pages for several Asian and other companies, including Reconnaissance Energy, Restaurant Brands Asia, Asia Pacific Wire & Cable and Asia Fiber, with no substantive news content.
A Borr Drilling rig sank off Gabon, with one person dead and four missing. Borr Drilling shares fell after the rig sank.
Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado returned after months in exile, greeted by supporters, as doubts over democracy deepen.
Brazil held a tense presidential runoff between Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro. Flavio Bolsonaro cast his ballot, and Lula later called Bolsonaro's exit from Brazil shameful after defeat.
Lula won Brazil's presidential election by a surprise margin but will face a hostile Congress and a polarised country.
Yasuo Fukuda, Japan's first second-generation prime minister, died at 90, according to a Nikkei report.
events.disputed: Reported by Nikkei via Reuters; not independently confirmed in the snippets.

events.summary: Microsoft is offering buyouts to around 60,000 employees to contain costs.
The Milwaukee Brewers routed the Rays 10-1 to move within a win of their first World Series title, with fans flooding Milwaukee streets for celebrations.
Trump and Rubio plan to visit an oil tanker in Texas carrying Venezuelan crude, touted as a record oil deal; reports note reality is setting in.

events.story: bank of canada rate hike expected

events.summary: Senior doctors in England are set to strike in November over a pay offer.
A judge ruled that the Trump Justice Department illegally fired Maurene Comey, daughter of former FBI director, as a federal prosecutor.
Swiss foreign minister is set to hold talks in North Korea this week on security issues.
events.story: swiss foreign minister north korea talks

events.summary: Global leaders have congratulated Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on his reelection as Brazil's president.
A machete-wielding mob attacked health workers responding to an Ebola outbreak in Congo.

events.summary: Brazil reelected Lula, and BBC reports his comeback dents Trump's ambitions for Latin America, though the Trump-Lula relationship may have thawed.
Jordan carried out a deadly strike in Syria in retaliation for a church attack, killing five people including women and children, Syrian health officials said.
events.disputed: Casualty figure is attributed to Syrian health officials.

events.summary: Tanzania has announced its first natural gas discovery in more than 10 years, which officials celebrated.
Africa CDC's Jean Kaseya warns the unprecedented Ebola outbreak could reach the UK and other countries unless more funding secures preparedness and treatment.
Zambia's president has appointed a new mines minister in cabinet changes following the election.
Namibia has raised its key interest rate to cushion second-round effects from high fuel prices.
European natural gas prices topped €100 per megawatt hour for the first time since the 2022 energy crisis, with storage only 72 percent full.
Putin met African leaders at a Moscow summit aimed at expanding Russia's ties with African countries.
Putin praised Elon Musk's genius and said he was in touch with Starlink's controlling shareholder as Russia plans its own satellite communications system.
events.disputed: Snippet describes Russia's plans to build a Starlink version as aimed at helping attack Ukraine, a characterization not independently verified in the text.

events.summary: Defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro and his family landed in Miami after leaving Brazil, and he says he will lead the opposition from the US.
events.story: flavio bolsonaro miami after election loss

events.summary: With over 90% of votes counted in Israel, results point to an election impasse, with new elections considered the most likely outcome.
Cost-of-living concerns over high food and energy costs are shaping US midterm elections, with the economy the top issue for most voters.
Egypt's central bank raised interest rates for the first time since March 2024, according to a Reuters headline.
ECB President Christine Lagarde will step down several months early to have more freedom to speak on matters that are not monetary policy, a move that will fuel speculation about her future plans.

Actor Patrick Stewart has died at age 86 after a brief journey with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia, The Guardian reports. He was known for Star Trek and X-Men roles and a long stage career.
Cuban voters who backed President Trump may now direct frustration at Republican immigration policies, the BBC reports.
A cross-party committee of MPs says the UK government's pledge to reverse obesity rates within a decade is doomed to fail without a major rethink and personal leadership from the PM.
Northern Ireland's PSNI police will reduce their response to non-emergency mental health call-outs.
France's economy unexpectedly shrank in the third quarter while inflation rose more than expected, and the finance minister warned the economy is headed for a wall, ahead of nationwide protests.
Maddie McCuddy, 23, from the US won the 2026 Ian Parry photojournalism grant, receiving £10,000, Canon equipment and mentorship; other new talents were also recognised.
China's central bank is shifting toward an overnight rate as its policy anchor, a change Reuters says signals easier funding conditions.
events.story: china central bank overnight rate shift

events.summary: Australia's central bank lifted rates to an 18-year high, with a split vote pointing to a pause ahead; separately, Uganda's inflation rose to a 3-year high after a currency slump.
Anticipation is building ahead of the finale of The Celebrity Traitors, according to BBC News.
The Guardian asked writers about the non-horror films that scared them most.
Brazil's President Lula is set to attend the UN COP31 climate summit in Turkey, Reuters reports.
Dockworkers in Europe and beyond are striking against arms shipments and over war deaths, with demands for better working conditions reported by AP.
An inquest found that Party Rock Anthem singer Lauren Bennett, who featured on LMFAO's hit song, struggled with mental health before her death.
North Korea says sanctions do not work to deny its status as a nuclear weapons state.
King visits the site of the 1823 Demerara slave rebellion in Guyana during a Caribbean tour; hundreds of slaves were killed in the rebellion.
Poland's Foreign Minister Sikorski calls for a rapid ceasefire in the Black Sea to allow food shipments.
Binance resumed crypto withdrawals after a major hack of $6.3 billion in tokens, which the FBI has tied to North Korea; Binance said it covered 95% of the stolen tokens.
events.disputed: North Korea's role is an accusation; the BBC notes the claims are not yet confirmed as true.

events.summary: Colombia's central bank held its interest rate and will shore up reserves with $2 billion, Reuters reports.
AP has published results pages for the 2026 US Senate, House and governor races.
Egypt's foreign minister says Egypt fears that an escalation in the Iran war would be more destructive.
The Cop17 UN biodiversity summit, focused on nature and ecosystems, concludes Saturday as critics call for reforms because countries are off track on nature targets.
events.disputed: Critics' claims that the summit system lets one country stall progress are presented as opinion.

events.summary: Environmental campaigners staged a Halloween-themed protest against fossil fuels at Bute House, the first minister's residence in Edinburgh.
More than 5,000 people have died from Ebola in DR Congo, the deadliest outbreak of the disease in the country.
Starved residents of Russian-occupied Oleshky returned to Ukraine during a rare local ceasefire.
events.disputed: Ukraine says the ceasefire was cover for Russian regrouping; this is a one-sided claim.

events.summary: On Brazil's election day, when buses stopped running, 'Lula's Army' grabbed their car keys to help voters.
US and Canada see growing interest in a limited ceasefire in the Black Sea.
Ghana says Russia will back a 2,000 MW nuclear plant and deepen ties between the two countries.
Alder Hey hospital has admitted responsibility for the death of a girl from Mold.
Palantir shares dropped after its earnings report, while Wall Street analysts remain bullish on the company and on two other stocks for the long term.
Tributes have been paid to Marta Shahbazi, a University of Cambridge scientist who died in a Spanish train crash, described by her laboratory as inspiring, talented and passionate.
Israeli strikes killed people in Gaza, according to medics, with reports giving differing death tolls of four and eight.
events.disputed: Reports give conflicting death tolls of four and eight, attributed to medics.

events.summary: Armed police have begun patrolling Sydney as a security measure after last year's deadly shooting attack at a Hanukkah festival at Bondi Beach.
Connecticut Senator Chris Murphy is in the hospital after having a stroke, according to his office.
The UN peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara has ended after 35 years, following an impasse between the US and Russia at the UN.
18-year-old violinist Sofia Demetriades won the BBC Young Musician 2026 competition.
An arrest has been made in a Holyhead murder case after police attended a medical emergency.
A business jet carrying nine people crashed in a Florida neighborhood on Sunday, erupting in a fireball, and all nine people on board died, according to US authorities.
events.story: florida business jet crash nine dead

Fiji's Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka faces pressure as his coalition reportedly falls apart ahead of a crucial third reading of a bill amending the 2013 Constitution.
Samoan Prime Minister La'auli joined a pro-Israel parade in Apia over the weekend, breaking down in tears while linking his support for Israel to his Christian faith.
Turkish President Erdogan said South Korea could partner in Turkey's Sinop nuclear project, and the two countries agreed to cooperate in nuclear, defence and infrastructure.
The dollar fell ahead of US midterm elections as oil prices plummeted, while gold also fell as higher oil stoked inflation fears.

Pasifika voters in Aotearoa say this election is about basics such as affordable food, petrol and access to affordable health services.
India is evacuating thousands of people ahead of a second cyclone in a week.
Punk band Bad Brains discuss drugs, self-destruction, claims they incited riots, and recording from jail in an interview with The Guardian.
Gold rose over 2% from a one-year low as oil prices softened, with investors focused on the US midterm elections.
Apple's new CEO Ternus faces its first earnings test as memory chip costs rise sharply.
Wage protests in Bangladesh have forced hundreds of garment factories to shut again, with some protests turning violent; the factories supply brands such as H&M and Uniqlo.
Samira's 16-year-old daughter Sevda was shot dead during mass protests in Iran in January, and Samira is now facing the regime.

Binance users withdrew about $3.4-3.6 billion after the exchange reopened trading following a cyberattack linked to a North Korean group that compromised over $6 billion in digital assets.
events.disputed: The attack is described as linked to a North Korean group; the snippets do not confirm attribution.

events.summary: Actors Rhys Ifans and Laura Linney discuss their Parkinson's drama, which deals frankly with death and dying.
events.story: rhys ifans laura linney parkinson's drama

events.summary: Beatles road manager Mal Evans's posthumous memoir says meeting Elvis Presley was the biggest day of his years with the Beatles.
The BBC explains what is on the ballot in the 2026 midterm elections in the United States.
A new cyberattack on supermarket fridges has swept across Europe.
Iran says contacts over ending the war continue after talks finished with no breakthrough.

Martha Stewart said she 'really screwed up' with a Halloween costume dressed as a homeless person. She has deleted a photo of herself in torn clothes with dirt on her face, which promoted her candle collection.
Senegal is hosting Africa's first Olympic event as citizens battle a cost of living crisis.
events.story: senegal olympic event cost of living

events.summary: A Guardian writer explains why the film (500) Days of Summer is their feelgood movie, part of a series on rewatched comfort films that carries special romantic meaning.
Argentina's austerity-hit economy is reeling toward recession, a test for President Milei ahead of the 2027 vote.
Reuters reports, citing sources, that a newborn was among 15 people killed when the Myanmar military struck a maternity clinic and a school.
events.disputed: Casualty details are attributed to unnamed sources and are not independently confirmed in the snippets.

The US midterm campaign has ended with control of Congress at stake, and Trump faces the midterm verdict.
Uganda says it has started withdrawing peacekeeping troops that helped repel militants in Somalia.
Space has been found for 1,000 fridges amid a disposal crisis.
Iliana Yotova won Bulgaria's presidential election, promising to be a 'president of peace'. The campaign showed how divided Bulgarians are over the war in Ukraine and drone attacks in the Black Sea.

Amish communities in Pennsylvania are under scrutiny amid a measles outbreak, as Governor Josh Shapiro mounts an outreach program; members say people do not change minds.

Grammy-winning singer Ashanti talks ahead of her Australian tour about her marriage to Nelly, fan encounters on stage and her debut album's upcoming 25th anniversary.
